# WO-632: Antivirus blocks the Windows download and install (Defender, Malwarebytes)
Status: GO (immediate)
Vendor: claude
Agent: devops-engineer, then qa-security (review)
Kind: packaging
Tier: standard
Severity: HIGH
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Target release: 0.3.2
Source: field report docs/feedback/2026-11-13-windows-family-test.md (F1, F2).
Boundary: no evasion of security products. The goal is a build antivirus has fewer reasons to distrust, plus false-positive reports. Never obfuscate, pack or hide behaviour. Buying a certificate or service is Tier 3 (owner).

## Task
1. Identify the exact live artifact (release tag, file name, SHA-256) and the build workflow that made it.
2. Audit the build for known false-positive triggers: the PyInstaller version and whether the bootloader is the stock prebuilt one; onefile vs onedir; missing Windows version resource (company, product, description, version); the installer wrapper (Inno/NSIS) settings; any bundled tool that self-extracts to %TEMP%.
3. Make the safe build changes in `packaging/windows/` and the release workflow: bootloader built from source in CI, full version resource, onedir inside the installer if not already, a reproducible build note. No functional change to the app.
4. Draft the false-positive submissions (Microsoft Security Intelligence "submit a file", Malwarebytes false-positive form) as text in `docs/release/AV_FALSE_POSITIVE.md`, ready for the owner to send. Sending is the owner's action.
5. Write a one-page signing options note (Azure Trusted Signing, OV/EV certificate, SignPath reapply after 1.0) with prices and sources, for an owner decision. Do not buy anything.
6. Update user help (Windows install page) only if wording about the warning is wrong; plain words per docs/POSITIONING.md.

## Acceptance
- The build changes pass CI on `windows-latest` (or are ready with exact steps if CI cannot run from here).
- AV_FALSE_POSITIVE.md and the signing note exist with sources.
- qa-security has reviewed the build changes. No AV evasion technique anywhere.
